Implementation Plan

I measured relative step weights locally and checked the existing step-move contracts. The plan is below.

## Planning ref
- Planning ref: `main` at `88de9d5ad723d0c0fbfee0848be0cc7e54e36db7`. The integration-branch mismatch flag reads `unknown`, not `true`, so there is no mismatch block. The `isolated-base` snapshot matches the working tree for every file read here.

## Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`
- `changelog.d/9420-ci-heal-job-steps-to-hooks-job.md` (new)

## Acceptance
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py::MovedHeal9420StepsContractTest red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py::MovedReleaseToHealStepsContractTest
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py
ACCEPTANCE: check tests-heal-plan-and-validation
ACCEPTANCE: check tests-hooks-and-orchestrator
ACCEPTANCE: post-merge workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml job tests-heal-plan-and-validation

## Evidence and choice of target
- On run 43314513853, `tests-heal-plan-and-validation` took 15m35s of its 20 minutes. The broker's step results for that run have statuses only, with no durations, so the choice of steps is an estimate, not a measurement.
- Measured in the planning sandbox, which has `python3` but no pytest or PyYAML:
  - `tests/test_pr_checks_lib_required_filter.py`: about 15s (64 tests).
  - `tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py`: about 11s before a test needing PyYAML stopped it (31 tests, 10 subprocess sites).
  - `tests/test_release_ci_gate.py`: about 6s. The step also runs 24 inline stubbed-`gh` cases of `scripts/release_ci_gate.sh` and a YAML check.
  - `tests/test_merge_probe.py`: about 3s, and 13 of its 14 tests passed. It has 27 `git` subprocess sites in temp repos.
  - The validation shell-quoting step has 6 modules, 3 pytest processes and 15 subprocess sites.
  - `tests/test_ci_cancelled_rerun.py` has 101 tests.
- The job's own `Workflow failure heal contract and driver tests` step is the job's largest cost. It cannot move whole: under #7387 it needed more than 7 minutes in another job and that job hit its timeout. #9045 already split it into 4 local shards. So the steps that move are the heaviest of the unsplit, unconditional steps.
- Target: `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`. Its last budget-watch record was 15m32s (run 43220859648, #9391). #9391 then moved its heaviest step out: `Pre-push affected-test gate tests`, about 472 tests in 10 serial pytest runs. That step alone was enough to tip orchestrate-poll group 3 to 15m17s (#9639).
- Other jobs have less room:
  - `tests-release-and-log-analysis` was at 15m19s (#9450) and lost only a ~162s step.
  - orchestrate-poll group 3 is flagged (#9639), and open PR #9641 moves a heavy step into group 0.
  - `tests-promote-stall-and-review` already ran 12.8 minutes in #7387.
  - `tests-system-python` and `tests-sandbox-python` exist to run on specific interpreters and are not general-purpose targets.
- The original plan for #9420 named the hooks job too: the granted changelog file is `9420-ci-heal-job-steps-to-hooks-job`.

## Functions or modules to implement
1. In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, cut these six steps from `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`. Keep each step's `name:` and `run:` body byte-for-byte; none has `if:`, `env:` or `continue-on-error:`.
   - `Merge probe unit tests`
   - `Validation shell-quoting and credential-scrub tests`
   - `Shared PR check-runs merge gate (pr_checks_lib) tests`
   - `Mark-stable release-tag refspec contract test`
   - `Release CI gate tests (stubbed gh; both release workflows)`
   - `Cancelled CI sweep recovery tests`
2. Append them, in that relative order, to the end of `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, after its last step `Clarify loop guard unit tests`. They are unguarded and run once per CI run.
3. Move the existing #8208 comment block that sits above `Mark-stable release-tag refspec contract test` along with the last three steps, and extend it. Above the first moved step, add one comment block saying:
   - The steps moved from `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`, which took 15m35s of its 20 minutes (run 43314513853, budget-watch issue #9420, re-issued as #9684).
   - The run's step timings were not readable, so the pick is an estimate from planning-sandbox timings and test and subprocess counts.
   - The heal step itself cannot move (#7387).
   - The steps need only the checkout, Python 3.12 and the job's pip set: no Node, no git history and no `.claude/` live copies.
   - The hooks job's extra base history is harmless to them.
   - Names and bodies are unchanged.
   - If budget-watch flags the hooks job next, measure step timings before moving anything again.
4. In the heal job, where the steps were, add a one-line comment for each removed group saying it "moved on to tests-hooks-and-orchestrator in #9420". This follows the existing "moved on to … in #8279" lines.
5. In `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`:
   - Set `RELEASE_TO_HEAL_TARGET_JOB_ID` to `"tests-hooks-and-orchestrator"` and keep the constant name, with the comment `# moved on to tests-hooks-and-orchestrator in budget-watch issue #9420; constant name kept`. This follows the `HEAL_TO_HOOKS_TARGET_JOB_ID` precedent.
   - Leave the test method names of `MovedReleaseToHealStepsContractTest` unchanged. Update its docstring to note the #9420 move.
6. Add constants and a new class `MovedHeal9420StepsContractTest`, modelled on `MovedRelease9450StepsContractTest` and `MovedHooks9391StepsContractTest`. It asserts that:
   - each of the six steps is owned only by `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`;
   - no moved step has an `if` key;
   - each step's `run` still names its modules, and those files exist;
   - no moved step is left in `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`;
   - in the hooks job, each step runs after `Install Python CI dependencies`, and the steps keep their relative order;
   - both jobs keep `timeout-minutes: 20`;
   - the target is not the source.

   The new constants are `HEAL_9420_SOURCE_JOB_ID`, `HEAL_9420_TARGET_JOB_ID`, `HEAL_9420_SETUP_STEP`, `HEAL_9420_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` and `MOVED_HEAL_9420_STEPS`. A search found no existing `9420` identifier in the file.
7. Add the changelog fragment `changelog.d/9420-ci-heal-job-steps-to-hooks-job.md`:
   - It starts with `<!-- changelog: changed -->`.
   - One bullet says which steps moved and why, that names, bodies and timeouts are unchanged, and that no job was added.
   - It ends with `Refs #9684, #9420`, using non-closing wording.

## Data structures affected
- `MOVED_HEAL_9420_STEPS` (new) maps each step name to the module paths its body names:
  - `Merge probe unit tests`: `tests/test_merge_probe.py`
  - `Validation shell-quoting and credential-scrub tests`: `tests/test_render_validation_templates_shell_quoting.py`, `tests/test_validate_driver_credential_scrub.py`, `tests/test_validation_streaming_output.py`, `tests/test_validate_scheduled_mode.py`, `tests/test_validate_scheduled_sink.py`, `tests/test_validate_presetup_cleanup_contract.py`
  - `Shared PR check-runs merge gate (pr_checks_lib) tests`: `tests/test_pr_checks_lib_required_filter.py`
  - `Mark-stable release-tag refspec contract test`: `tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py`
  - `Release CI gate tests (stubbed gh; both release workflows)`: `tests/test_release_ci_gate.py`
  - `Cancelled CI sweep recovery tests`: `tests/test_ci_cancelled_rerun.py`
- `RELEASE_TO_HEAL_TARGET_JOB_ID` keeps its name; only its value changes.
- No workflow job ids, step names, timeouts, matrices, triggers or permissions change.

## API or interface changes
- None. Check-run names are job ids and stay the same. Neither job is renamed or added. The `lint` aggregate `needs:` list is unchanged.

## Decisions
### D1 — Target `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`
- Chosen: append the moved steps to `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`.
- Alternatives considered: `tests-release-and-log-analysis` (15m19s in #9450, minus a ~162s step); an orchestrate-poll group (group 3 is flagged in #9639, and #9641 loads group 0); `tests-promote-stall-and-review`; splitting the move across two jobs as #8993 and #9018 did.
- Why: this job lost the heaviest step any recent move took out (#9391, about 472 tests). That step was big enough to tip another job by itself, so this job has the most room. It also matches the granted changelog name. One target keeps the diff and any merge conflicts small.

### D2 — Move all three #8208 steps together
- Chosen: move `Mark-stable…`, `Release CI gate…` and `Cancelled CI sweep recovery tests` as a group and repoint `RELEASE_TO_HEAL_TARGET_JOB_ID`.
- Alternatives considered: move only two of them and change `MOVED_RELEASE_TO_HEAL_STEPS` into a per-step `(job, modules)` map.
- Why: the existing contract pins all three to a single target constant. Moving them together needs a one-value edit instead of a restructured test.

### D3 — Do not re-shard or raise the timeout
- Chosen: move steps unchanged.
- Alternatives considered: raise `heal_shards` from 4; raise `timeout-minutes`.
- Why: the issue forbids raising the timeout and asks for steps to move unchanged. Changing the shard count changes a step body.

### D4 — Skip `Tracking issue comment cap tests`
- Chosen: leave it in the heal job.
- Alternatives considered: move it as well.
- Why: #7366 moved it out of the hooks job for that job's budget, so moving it back would undo that move.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: none change. Every moved step runs in a job with the same `ubuntu-latest` runner and the same default `GITHUB_TOKEN` scope, and no step uses a secret. The hooks job already exposes `pull-requests: read` for its base-fetch step, and the moved steps do not read it.
- Final-CI runs: the hooks job runs `Verify the final-CI merge ref is current`, just as the heal job does, so the moved steps keep testing the merge ref.
- External input: the moved steps take no PR-con
